basics.name: Cesar Ramos
basics.label: Economist · M.Sc. candidate in Policy Economics, Williams College
basics.summary: Bolivian economist and M.Sc. candidate in Policy Economics at the Center for Development Economics, Williams College. Five years of econometric research and policy advisory work at Bolivia's Ministry of Economy and Public Finance, with research in macroeconomics, fiscal and monetary policy, heterogeneous agents, applied econometrics and machine learning.

work.name: Fiscal Analysis and Studies Unit (economic policy advisory unit), Ministry of Economy and Public Finance (MEFP)
work.position: Econometric researcher; economic and data analyst (econometrics/ML)
work.summary: Research on the fiscal, real, financial, price and external sectors, applying econometric tools to provide evidence on the impact of economic policies.
highlights: Designed and executed economic and statistical analyses using macro/financial datasets to support fiscal and macro policy decisions.
Developed forecasting and monitoring (time series, nowcasting, scenario analysis) and translated results into policy briefs, reports, dashboards and presentations for senior stakeholders.
Implemented reproducible pipelines: ETL, model estimation, and documentation for recurring reports.
Managed the drafting, review, editing and publication of the Cuadernos de Investigación Económica Boliviana (CIEB) journal.
Coordinated technical work with other institutions and shared analytical results.

work.name: MEFP (Bolivia) & Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)
work.position: Econometrics & Machine-Learning Lead Analyst – Social Registry of Households Roadmap
highlights: Co-authored Annex 2 on household prioritization using Proxy Means Testing (PMT).
Developed, estimated, and validated OLS and machine-learning models used in the annex.

work.name: Journal Análisis Económico, Universidad Alberto Hurtado
highlights: Reviewed economics manuscripts and provided methodological and empirical feedback to support editorial decisions.

work.name: CIIP LATAM – Integral Center for Research and Professional Training
highlights: Macroeconometrics and advanced macro data analysis.
Development econometrics and panel data analysis: models for decision-making.
Bayesian econometrics and econometrics for forecasting with machine learning and deep learning.
